served.stem: Catalytic hydrogenation (H2/Pd) of the cyclic alkene shown is performed. What is the major organic product of this reaction?
served.bankWhy: H2/Pd adds two H across the single C=C of cyclohexene to give saturated cyclohexane. No O or halogen is introduced, and benzene (more unsaturated) is not formed by reduction.

answer.line: H2 and Pd add one H to each alkene carbon and nothing else. The C=C is gone: cyclohexane.

steps: Read the reagent. H2 with a metal catalyst brings hydrogen, and only hydrogen.
Add one H to each alkene carbon, both from the same face, off the metal surface.
No O and no Br came in, and the ring stays a ring. The product is cyclohexane.

choices.note: Adding H and OH is hydration, with acid and water or with hydroboration. This flask has only H2.
Benzene would mean taking hydrogen away. Hydrogenation adds it.
Two Br atoms across the C=C is what Br2 adds. A different reagent.
Two H across the C=C, nothing else: the alkane.
A ketone needs an oxygen brought in, by hydration and then oxidation. H2 and Pd bring none.
